🌋 Godzilla Docs
  • Authentication
  • Getting Started
  • Installation
  • Quickstart

Quickstart

The fastest path from zero to a running pipeline.

1. Set up your client and API key

Follow the Installation guide to install an SDK or configure direct API access, and see Authentication if you need to generate an API key.

2. Create a pipeline

terminal bash 
curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"name":"my-first-pipeline","source_connector_id":"conn_demo_source","destination_connector_id":"conn_demo_dest"}'
create_pipeline.go go 
client := godzilla.NewClient(os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY"))

pipeline, err := client.Pipelines.Create(ctx, &godzilla.PipelineCreateParams{
    Name:                   "my-first-pipeline",
    SourceConnectorID:      "conn_demo_source",
    DestinationConnectorID: "conn_demo_dest",
})

3. Watch it run

Subscribe to pipeline.completed via Webhooks, or poll the Events endpoint to see events as they're processed.

That's it

For a fuller walkthrough with a real source and destination, go to Building your first pipeline in the Guides section.

args.content:
🌋 Godzilla Docs
  • Authentication
  • Getting Started
  • Installation
  • Quickstart

Installation

Godzilla has no server to install — it's a hosted platform you reach over the REST API, either directly or through an SDK.

Option A: Use an SDK

terminal bash 
npm install @godzilla/sdk
# or
pip install godzilla-sdk
# or
go get github.com/godzilla/godzilla-go

Full setup for each is in Go SDK, Node.js SDK, and Python SDK.

Option B: Call the API directly

No install needed — every endpoint in the API reference is a plain HTTPS request.

terminal bash 
curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"
Next

Either way, you'll need an API key before you can make a request — see Authentication, or jump straight into the Quickstart to create your first pipeline.
